raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Add the Ascend A3 deployment scenarios requested in Ascend/sglang#1206 to the DeepSeek-R1 Cookbook, so you can select a scenario and get the matching launch command: one complete A3 server with PD co-located, or two A3 servers with PD disaggregated (Prefill, Decode and Router).

This change depends on #46270 for grouped ModelSlim W4A8 loading.

## Modifications

- Add an `Ascend A3` hardware option to the existing Basic Configuration selector with two scenarios: 1×A3 with PD co-located, and 2×A3 with PD disaggregated (Prefill, Decode and Router roles). The generated commands follow the [official R1 W4A8 best practices](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/deepseek_r1.mdx) and use Cookbook ports (30000 for servers, 6688 for the Router). Host-specific values are placeholders: `<network-interface>`, `<prefill-ip>`, `<decode-ip>` and the model path.
- Add the A3 content to the sections the page already uses: `3.4 Ascend A3 deployment` (prerequisites, checkpoint, host tuning, network variables), `4.3 Verify the Ascend A3 service` (Router check and a request), and `5.3 Ascend A3 benchmarks` (the performance and GSM8K commands).
- Add generator tests for the A3 roles to the docs CI entry.

Three documentation files change: the R1 page, its existing selector component and the generator tests. No inference-runtime change.

## Accuracy Tests

Atlas 800T A3 x2 (driver 26.1.1, firmware 9.0.0.9.220), CANN 9.1.0, torch/torch_npu 2.10.0, MemFabric 1.2.1, Router 0.3.2, image `quay.io/ascend/sglang:main-cann9.1.0-a3` (manifest `sha256:9e653832d34f058a0035b5009fe8efcd61358c72fec5cf7412df7a236ff544ae`), SGLang `bb72b47` with the configuration and scale-layout fixes from #46270 (MoE TP=1), checkpoint revision `8c4f13004d0742b650b9f2c51b751dbef7d0c1ee`.

Full GSM8K test set (1319 questions, `sgl-eval==0.1.3`, thinking on, 16384 output tokens, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, seed 1, concurrency 64, context length 32768):

| Deployment | Correct | Score | Request errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1×A3, PD co-located | 1257/1319 | 95.30% | 0 |
| 2×A3, PD disaggregated | 1256/1319 | 95.22% | 0 |

The commands the page generates were launched unchanged on this setup (co-located, Prefill, Decode and Router). Functional checks (plain, streaming, multi-turn and 4 concurrent chat requests) passed for both deployments. For PD, the Router listed one healthy prefill and one healthy decode worker.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Three consecutive runs of the best-practice benchmark against one running service, with no restart or tuning between runs. Mean TPOT per run:

| Deployment | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Average | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Co-located (896 req, concurrency 224) | 50.77 | 53.06 | 54.13 | 52.65 ms | 50 ms |
| PD (1664 req, concurrency 416, 24 req/s) | 47.88 | 46.17 | 46.27 | 46.77 ms | 50 ms |

All 7680 measured requests completed. PD is below the reference in every run, and co-located averages slightly above it. The reference defines no multi-run aggregation rule.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit guide (`pre-commit run --all-files` on the full tree: returncode 0, 31 passed).
- [x] Add unit tests (generator tests in `docs/scripts/tests/deepseek-r1-ascend.test.mjs`; the docs suite passes 61/61). In a headless browser on a local `mint dev`, every A3 role shows the generated command, the existing B200 command is unchanged, and the Advanced selector does not affect the Basic one.
- [x] Update documentation (this PR is the documentation).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -15,11 +15,12 @@ import { DeepSeekR1AdvancedDeployment } from '/src/snippets/autoregressive/deeps - **Advanced Reasoning**: Built-in reasoning capabilities for complex problem-solving - **Multiple Quantizations**: FP8 and FP4 variants for different performance/memory trade-offs -- **Hardware Optimization**: Specifically tuned for NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell) and H200 (Hopper) GPUs, AMD MI300X, MI325X and MI355X GPUs, as well as Intel Xeon CPUs +- **Hardware Optimization**: Specifically tuned for NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell) and H200 (Hopper) GPUs, AMD MI300X, MI325X and MI355X GPUs, as well as Intel Xeon CPUs and Ascend A3 NPUs - **High Performance**: Optimized for both throughput and latency scenarios **Available Models:** +- **Ascend A3 ModelSlim W4A8**: [Modelers_Park/DeepSeek-R1-0528-w4a8](https://modelers.cn/Modelers_Park/DeepSeek-R1-0528-w4a8) — use the Ascend A3 selection below; this checkpoint uses a different format from the W4AFP8 checkpoint listed below. - **FP8 (8-bit quantized)**: [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528) - Recommended for H200 and MI300X - **FP4 (4-bit quantized)**: [nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4-v2](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-0528-FP4-v2) - Recommended for B200 and MI355X - **BF16 (upcast from FP8)**: [unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-0528-BF16](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-0528-BF16) @@ -79,6 +80,10 @@ DeepSeek-R1 shares the same MoE architecture as DeepSeek-V3, so the same hardwar INT8 16× A100/A800, 32× L40S, Xeon 6980P CPU, 4× Ascend A3 Series + + W4A8 (ModelSlim) + Ascend A3: 1 server (8 cards, 16 devices) for PD co-located; 2 servers for PD disaggregated + W4A8 / AWQ / MXFP4 / NVFP4 8× H20/H100, 4× H200; 8× H100/A100; 8/4× MI355X/MI350X; 8/4× B200 @@ -99,6 +104,28 @@ python3 -m sglang.compile_deep_gemm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 --tp 8 --tru **Xeon CPU service configuration:** Please refer to the `Notes` part in the serving engine launching section in [the SGLang CPU server document](../../../docs/hardware-platforms/cpu_server#launch-of-the-serving-engine) to better understand how to configure the arguments, especially for TP (tensor parallel) and NUMA binding settings. +### 3.4 Ascend A3 deployment + +Select **Ascend A3** in the Basic Configuration selector above. Then choose **1×A3 · PD co-located**, or choose **2×A3 · PD disaggregated** and a **Prefill**, **Decode**, or **Router** role. An A3 server has 8 cards (16 logical devices), and in the disaggregated recipe each node runs a full TP16 copy of the model. The generated commands follow the [official R1 W4A8 best practices](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/deepseek_r1) and use the same `python3 -m sglang.launch_server` entry point as the other commands on this page. + +Before launching: + +1. Use an SGLang build that includes the grouped ModelSlim W4A8 loading fix. Without it, this checkpoint produces invalid output. +2. Pull the A3 image with `docker pull quay.io/ascend/sglang:main-cann9.1.0-a3`. Set up a container with a matched driver, CANN, TorchNPU, and MemFabric by following the [Ascend installation guide](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation). Mount all 16 devices and the model directory. +3. Download the [ModelSlim W4A8 checkpoint](https://modelers.cn/Modelers_Park/DeepSeek-R1-0528-w4a8) (about 403 GB) on every node. It includes the NextN/MTP weights used by the speculative-decoding settings. +4. Apply the host tuning from the best practice on each host: + + ```bash + echo performance | tee \ + /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor + sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 kernel.numa_balancing=0 \ + kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 + ``` + +5. Replace the placeholders in the command. Use your host network interface for ``. For disaggregation, use the Prefill host address for `` and the Decode host address for ``. Prefill creates the MemFabric store at `:24670`, so start Prefill and Decode first and the Router last. The Router listens on port `6688`. The `8998` after `--prefill` in the Router command is the Prefill bootstrap port, so keep it equal to the Prefill `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`. + +After the service starts, [verify it](#4-3-verify-the-ascend-a3-service) and [run the benchmarks](#5-3-ascend-a3-benchmarks). + ## 4. Model Invocation ### 4.1 Basic Usage @@ -373,6 +400,37 @@ response = client.chat.completions.create( print(response) ``` +### 4.3 Verify the Ascend A3 service + +Wait for the server to finish loading the weights and capturing graphs. Then check the service from another terminal in the same container. For the disaggregated recipe, the Router listens on port `6688`, and its `/workers` endpoint must list one healthy `prefill` and one healthy `decode` worker: + +```bash Command +curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 30 \ + http://127.0.0.1:6688/workers +``` + +Send a request through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: + +```python Example +from openai import OpenAI + +client = OpenAI( + base_url="http://127.0.0.1:6688/v1", api_key="EMPTY", +) +model = client.models.list().data[0].id +response = client.chat.completions.create( + model=model, + messages=[ + {"role": "user", "content": "What is 7 multiplied by 8?"}, + ], + temperature=0, + max_tokens=1024, +) +print(response.choices[0].message.content) +``` + +For the co-located recipe, use `http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1` instead. + ## 5. Benchmark This section uses **industry-standard configurations** for comparable benchmark results. @@ -991,3 +1049,47 @@ Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 29.185 s Output throughput: 4854.672 token/s ``` + +### 5.3 Ascend A3 benchmarks + +Use the generated A3 commands for both the performance and the accuracy runs. + +#### 5.3.1 Performance + +The [Ascend best practice](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/deepseek_r1) lists 50 ms TPOT for both deployments. Run the benchmark against the running service, and add `--dataset-path` with a local ShareGPT file if the host is offline. + +```bash Command +# 1×A3, PD co-located +python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --dataset-name random --backend sglang \ + --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \ + --max-concurrency 224 --num-prompts 896 \ + --random-input-len 3500 --random-output-len 1500 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 --seed 1 +``` + +```bash Command +# 2×A3, PD disaggregated (through the Router) +python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --dataset-name random --backend sglang \ + --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \ + --max-concurrency 416 --num-prompts 1664 --request-rate 24 \ + --random-input-len 3584 --random-output-len 1536 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 --seed 1 +``` + +Compare the mean TPOT with the reference. The two deployments use different workloads, so do not compare their throughput with each other. If you need to reach the reference value, tune the host and scheduling settings for your own system. + +#### 5.3.2 GSM8K accuracy + +Restart the generated command with `--context-length 32768`, then run the full test set. Set `MODEL_ID` to the name returned by `/v1/models`, set `GSM8K_TEST_JSONL` to the GSM8K test set in the `sgl-eval` input format, set `EVAL_OUTPUT` to a directory for the results, and use the Router URL (`http://127.0.0.1:6688/v1`) for the disaggregated deployment. + +```bash Command +sgl-eval run gsm8k \ + --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \ + --model "$MODEL_ID" \ + --from-dataset "$GSM8K_TEST_JSONL" \ + --num-examples 1319 --num-threads 64 --n-repeats 1 \ + --temperature 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --seed 1 --thinking \ + --max-tokens 16384 --out-dir "$EVAL_OUTPUT" +```
